chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Abi al-Jawza', from al-Husayn ibn 'Ulwan, from 'Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn 'Ali, from his father, from his forefathers, from 'Ali عليه السلام, who said:
The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم was asked about the sorcerer, so he said: “If two just men come and testify against him, then his blood has become lawful.”

key_terms.السَّاحِرِ: the sorcerer; a practitioner of sorcery under legal discussion
key_terms.حَلَّ دَمُهُ: his blood became lawful; he became liable to lawful execution
key_terms.رَجُلَانِ: two men; the number of witnesses required here
key_terms.عَدْلَانِ: just and upright; describing qualified witnesses
key_terms.فَشَهِدَا: they testified; gave formal witness testimony

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a sorcerer if two just witnesses testify against him?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم concerning the sorcerer. It indicates that upon the testimony of two just witnesses against him, capital punishment becomes applicable, reflecting a judicial ruling tied to evidentiary standards.
